## Parent

#1090

## What to build

Make lock timeout, statement timeout, cancellation during refresh, and scheduler error/recovery tests witness the fault they claim to test. Use nonempty committed input and controlled sessions, observe the operation at its blocker or fault point, check published state immediately after failure, and compare exact state after recovery. Record whether the refresh used a differential or full path. Use dedicated instances for disruptive operations and clean up locks and session settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each scenario witnesses the intended fault and checks immediate state and recovery; unrelated errors do not count.
- [ ] Removing the blocker, cancelling the wrong backend, or disabling the fault makes the relevant test fail. Sleep alone does not establish overlap.
- [ ] A bounded repeated run stays reliable under normal CI concurrency, retains initial failures, and leaves no session or server state behind.
- [ ] Exact result checks use #1091 when available; session and fault-helper work can start independently.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Historical context

Replaces the retained scope of #1045 and the named failure schedules in #1052.

---

<!-- acceptance-matrix:1092 -->
## Detailed acceptance matrix

These rows define the evidence required for acceptance. They do not claim completed verification.

### #1092: witnessed failures and recovery

Anchors: [failure recovery](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/tests/e2e_failure_recovery_tests.rs),
[scheduler failpoint case](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/tests/e2e_dvm_failpoint_tests.rs), and
[chaos setup](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/tests/e2e_cleanup_chaos_tests.rs).
Keep the existing four required case identities below when strengthening them.

| ID | Source | Requirement and scope | Boundaries / counterexamples | Evidence type | Exact evidence | Done |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1092-R01 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1 | The lock-timeout case observes a refresh blocked by its intended blocker and then a lock timeout. | No conflicting lock, wrong backend, unrelated SQL error, or refresh success. | behavioral test | E: `e2e_failure_recovery_tests::test_lock_timeout_during_refresh`. Use committed pending input, pinned blocker/refresher connections, and a relation the refresh actually accesses. Require blocker PID in `pg_blocking_pids(refresh_pid)` and target SQLSTATE `55P03` from the refresh. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R02 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1 | The statement-timeout case observes the refresh in progress and receives the intended statement timeout. | `lock_timeout` fires first or the statement completes normally. | behavioral test | E: `e2e_failure_recovery_tests::test_statement_timeout_during_refresh_recovers`. Set `lock_timeout=0` and the statement timeout on the pinned target session. Observe a controlled wait inside refresh, then require SQLSTATE `57014` and its statement-timeout diagnostic. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R03 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1 | Cancellation interrupts the observed target refresh. | `pg_cancel_backend` returns true after work finished, or cancels an unrelated session. | behavioral test | E: `e2e_failure_recovery_tests::test_cancel_backend_during_refresh_recovers`. Record target PID, witness its active refresh at a controlled wait, cancel it, and require the target statement's `57014` cancellation error. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R04 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1 | A scheduler-owned attempt encounters the selected injected failure. | Only an error counter changes, no pending committed input, or a manual call substitutes for scheduler execution. | behavioral test | E: strengthen `e2e_dvm_failpoint_tests::test_dvm_failpoint_preserves_last_committed_result_and_recovers`. Require pending journaled input, scheduler/backend identity, a reached fault marker, and the corresponding failure diagnostic. Record if the chosen fault is before apply; it supplies no #1094 after-apply evidence. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R05 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1 | Each failed attempt preserves the last committed public result and successful progress immediately after failure. | A later successful refresh repairs corruption before the assertion. | behavioral test | E: the four cases above capture S immediately after the witnessed fault. Public rows and successful progress equal the saved baseline; any permitted scheduler error diagnostics are recorded separately. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R06 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC1/AC4 | Recovery reaches the exact known committed result after the fault is removed. | Counts match while values differ, pending input is lost, or duplicate effects appear. | behavioral test | E: all four cases use the repaired #1091 comparator against J or their preserved corpus checkpoint. The scheduler case must recover through a scheduler-owned attempt and reset its consecutive-error count. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R07 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W | Evidence identifies the actual refresh path attempted. | Requested DIFFERENTIAL mode is reported even though work used FULL or never reached apply. | invariant | P: `check_failure_attempt_path` in the four test diagnostics. Retain requested mode, reached phase, actual path/strategy when reached, and fallback reason. Failed transactions need an observable attempt marker because successful history rolls back. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R08 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W | Disruptive tests cannot terminate or reconfigure another test's server. | Shared-container backend termination or leaked `ALTER SYSTEM` settings affect unrelated tests. | invariant | P: `check_disruption_instance_ownership`. The failure tests use `E2eDb::new_dedicated` for process/server-wide disruption and target recorded instance/backend identities only. Run alongside an independent sentinel instance whose query remains usable. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R09 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), W/AC3 | Fault teardown releases its locks, tasks, temporary resources, and session/server settings. | Pool-level RESET affects a different session; a pinned transaction or temporary relation survives. | behavioral test | E: strengthen `test_no_resource_leak_after_timeout`. After the observed fault, roll back and await tasks. On the same still-live backend, compare fixture temporary relations/locks/settings with baseline and run a clean operation. Clear server fault settings, release pinned sessions, then tear down the container. Session destruction must not hide a leak. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R10 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), AC2 | Disabling the intended fault makes the relevant failure test reject the run. | Removing the blocker, cancelling an idle wrong PID, or disabling scheduler injection still yields a pass. | behavioral test | P: `test_failure_witness_controls_reject_missing_fault`. Run these three controls against the same witness assertions used above. Require a missing-intended-fault failure; unrelated timeout or SQL failure does not satisfy it. | [ ] |
| Q1092-R11 | [#1092](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1092), AC3 | Repeated execution remains reliable without erasing earlier correctness failures. | A flaky failure is replaced by a passing retry or loses its logs. | invariant | P: `failure_schedule_repetition` in existing CI. Run ten attempts per named schedule under configured concurrency. Retain all outcomes and witnesses; any required correctness failure leaves the aggregate non-passing. #1093 validates that attempt history. | [ ] |
<!-- /acceptance-matrix:1092 -->

# PROVEN — #1092

Candidate: `404d08fe1452350926e6bc481d68d92e28bdb73a` (`codex/implement-1092`), clean and unchanged throughout verification.

Environment: rebuilt `pg_trickle_e2e:latest` from this workspace; PostgreSQL 18 E2E containers.

Checks:

- `just lint` — passed with zero warnings; `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused witness/control suite — 7/7 passed.
- Scheduler-chaos anchor — 1/1 passed.
- Ten supported CI-style repetitions with `--retries 0` — 10/10 attempts passed, 40/40 scheduled cases passed, and every attempt log was retained.

Acceptance matrix:

| ID | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Q1092-R01 | `test_lock_timeout_during_refresh` observed the pinned refresh waiting on its recorded blocker via `pg_blocking_pids`, required SQLSTATE `55P03`, preserved the checkpoint, and recovered exactly. | proven |
| Q1092-R02 | `test_statement_timeout_during_refresh_recovers` observed the controlled lock wait, required SQLSTATE `57014` with the statement-timeout diagnostic, preserved the checkpoint, and recovered. | proven |
| Q1092-R03 | `test_cancel_backend_during_refresh_recovers` cancelled the witnessed target PID, required SQLSTATE `57014` with the user-request diagnostic, preserved the checkpoint, and recovered. | proven |
| Q1092-R04 | `test_dvm_failpoint_preserves_last_committed_result_and_recovers` recorded committed pending input, scheduler ownership, `FAILED` history, SQLSTATE `40001`, the reached failpoint marker, suspension, and a later scheduler-owned successful recovery. | proven |
| Q1092-R05 | The four fault tests compare public state immediately after the witnessed failure against a pre-fault checkpoint; the scheduler test does the same before recovery. | proven |
| Q1092-R06 | Fault cases use the exact checkpoint oracle; scheduler recovery requires a later `COMPLETED` scheduler attempt with `consecutive_errors = 0` and direct-query equality. | proven |
| Q1092-R07 | Manual cases assert requested/refresh/effective `DIFFERENTIAL` path; the scheduler marker records phase, action, backend PID, and `actual_path=NOT_REACHED`. | proven |
| Q1092-R08 | Disruptive cases use dedicated instances; the sentinel test verifies a separate instance remains usable and does not inherit server settings. | proven |
| Q1092-R09 | Same-backend baseline/after snapshots cover session settings, temporary relations, and temporary locks; blockers are rolled back, fault settings are cleared, and clean refreshes succeed with no delta-table residue. | proven |
| Q1092-R10 | The negative-control test proves missing blocker, wrong cancellation PID, and disabled scheduler injection do not satisfy the intended-fault assertions. | proven |
| Q1092-R11 | The repetition schedule ran ten attempts per named schedule with no retries, retained every log, and returned aggregate success for all attempts. | proven |

No repair was necessary. The issue is fully proven against the candidate above.

title: Make timeout, cancellation, and scheduler-failure tests real
